Commentary.Commentary: That concludes our coverage for this game. It turned out to be a pretty one-sided affair much like the Test matches, although Bangladesh were the dominant side for a change. The venue for the second ODI remains the same but it will be a day-night contest. Do join us at 1430 local (1830 GMT) on 25th July for all the action. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Winning Bangladesh skipper, Mashrafe Mortaza says that it's tiring but his knee is alright. Says that he has not bowled much in the last few months but he enjoyed on the ground today. Adds that they just need to play with passion and whatever is gone is gone and they wanted to start well in this series. Hopes to carry the form forward. Reminds us that they won against South Africa in 2007 at this very ground and feels that the pitch here suits them. Praises Shakib and Tamim for their knocks and lauds Rahim's cameo as well.

Tamim Iqbal is the Man of the Match for his fine century. He says it was tough going for them and the first 10 overs were very difficult. Feels the wicket became easier to bat on after the 25th over. States that they had a score in mind and luckily Rahim played a handy cameo to take them there. Admits they didn't play good cricket in Tests but this is the format they play their best. Further adds that they wanted to play their 'A' game and is glad that they managed to do so.

Jason Holder, the Windies skipper, says that Bangladesh played some good cricket and rues their death bowling. Adds that they created chances as a bowling unit and needed partnerships while batting. Feels that they need to execute their plans well and bat better. Mentions about preparing well for the next game and talking about their plans. Is immediate to say that they had plans today also but it didn't work as they didn't hold on to their chances.

It was a sorry batting card for the hosts and the fact that their last wicket partnership was their best effort of the innings really tells the story. Credit should be given to the Bangladesh bowlers for the way they bowled. They executed their plan accurately and every bowler played his role. The tourists managed to create pressure right from the beginning which resulted in the fall of wickets at regular intervals. Earlier, the double century stand between Shakib and Tamim along with the cameo by Rahim powered Bangladesh to a challenging total. In fact, the quickfire stand between Rahim and Tamim in a way proved to the differential factor. Altogether, a convincing win for the Asian team to begin the series.

It wasn't an easy pitch for stroke making and once Bangladesh took their total past 250, it became even tougher for the home team. Despite having two powerhouses opening for them, Windies never got going. Chris Gayle adopted a cautious approach where he was concentrating more on the singles while Evin Lewis' stay was a short one. Shai failed to give enough hope and once Chris Gayle got run out, the run chase fell flat on its face. Shimron Hetmyer did try to revive his team's fortune by forming a few useful partnerships but he also departed soon after completing his half century.

Bangladesh taste their first success on this tour. The Test series was a dismal one for them but the change in leadership has brought them luck. Mashrafe Mortaza surely knows how to guide these bunch of boys and the skipper himself led from the front. In spite of not being fully fit, he bowled beautifully, mixing his pace and length, and finished with a 4-wicket haul. All in all, a clinical bowling performance by them, although the last wicket partnership put a little bit of blemish as it really tested their patience.

They have done it. Windies have done it. No they have not won the game but they have managed to not get bowled out. The last wicket partnership really frustrated the Bangla bowlers for 56 balls. The last delivery was a shorter one to which Bishoo swung his bat and missed. All over, BANGLADESH WIN BY 48 RUNS!
A low full toss on off, Bishoo presents the full face of the bat and pushes it back to the bowler.

Takes it on the full and drives it to mid off. Charges to the other end as Sabbir misses his shy at the bowler's end. They cross for an overthrow as well. The replays show that Bishoo would have been run out in case of a direct hit.

An off pace delivery, on a fuller length and angling down, Bishoo tries to play the reverse sweep but it takes the back of the bat, brushes his gloves and then loops behind. Falls well in front of the keeper though.
Hits the yorker mark this time, Bishoo digs it out safely.
A low full toss outside off, Joseph slices his drive through point for a single.
FOUR! Back of a length ball angling into the batsman, Bishoo swivels on the back leg and muscles his pull over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Bishoo goes for the pull but misses it completely.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
The batsman plays a pull shot to this short delivery. They pick up a single.

Is this it? Noooo... A wild slog by Bishoo. He gets a big top edge over mid-wicket and Sabbir runs behind it from the ring. Puts in a dive but to no avail. Two taken and that brings up the 50-run stand, first one of the innings. Wow.

FOUR! Misfield in the deep! Also that was crisply struck by Bishoo. He takes his front leg away from the line of the delivery and whips it down to wide long on. Mosaddek moves across to his left in the deep, puts in a dive to stop the ball but it's not cleanly done. It ends up rolling back to the rope.
Angles it wide outside off, Alzarri leaves it alone.
Bishoo will feel that he has been robbed off a boundary. He hammers a full ball straight back and it goes on to hit the stumps at the other end. The ball deflects and they cross.
Shortish and outside off, punched to extra cover.
Cutting back into the batsman from around middle, Bishoo fails to keep it out and is hit high on the pads.
Good length delivery outside off, Bishoo mistimes his shot to mid off.
Too full in length and outside off, Joseph hangs back and chips his shot square of the wicket on the off side. A single taken.
Good length ball on middle, Bishoo stays back and defends it watchfully.
On a length around off, Bishoo drives it to mid off.
Good length ball around leg, Alzarri swings his bat but misses. It goes behind off his thigh pad. They cross and it's given as a run. Maybe some inside edge.
Wide! Slips it down the leg side, Joseph swings and misses.
A cracking yorker, fantastic reply from Rubel. Alzarri does well though to keep it out.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Shortish ball on off, Joseph makes room and powers it through the line. That's struck with immense force and bursts through the hands of the mid off fielder. Mosaddek there probably took it too lightly. A boundary results.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and pushes it to covers for a run.
Fractionally short and outside off, Devendra stays back and steers it to sweeper cover for a single.
Bouncer around middle, Bishoo sways away from the line.
Angling down the leg side, slower in pace, Bishoo tries working it around the corner but misses.
Back of a length delivery outside off, thumped down the ground to long on for a run.
Top edge but safe. Bishoo brings out the reverse-batted shot. Fails to middle it properly and it goes on one bounce to third man. A single.
Slower one, on a length around off, Bishoo pushes at it and misses.
Mustafizur Rahman is back into the attack.
A length ball on middle, kept out from the inner half of the bat to the leg side.
FOUR! Joseph is showing his hitting range. Pushing for a promotion in the batting order. Lines himself up behind the delivery and bludgeons it straight down the ground for a boundary.
Full and in line of the stumps, Bishoo forces it down to long on and picks up a single. 200 up for Windies.
Full and straight, defended towards mid-wicket.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Flatter and on off, defended off the back foot.

SIX! Nails it! This one lands on a fuller length around off, not spinning much, Joseph this time goes straighter and clubs it over long on for a maximum. 18 from the over, the most expensive one of this run chase!
Fires this one in on middle, Alzarri stays back and keeps it out off the leading half of the bat.

Four byes! An arm ball landing around middle and leg and skidding down. Joseph once again winds up for a big shot across the line but misses. It misses the leg pole by a whisker and speeds away to the fine leg fence.
SIX! That's gone all the way! Flighted full around off, straightening a bit, Joseph goes through with the big swing of his bat and dispatches it over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Skidding down towards leg, Bishoo nudges it behind square leg for a run.
Drills it down to long off for a single.
Very full and on middle, kept out towards mid-wicket.
Rocks back and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Short and on middle, pulled towards mid-wicket.
Stays on the back foot and punches it to the leg side.
Stays back and punches it to covers for a single. The fielder misses his shy at the striker's end and with no one backing up, they cross for an overthrow.
Bishoo has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Arm ball on off, driven back to the bowler.
Tossed up ball on off, chipped over mid off for a single.
Mashrafe Mortaza is leaving the field. Walking a bit gingerly. He has done his job though and with just one wicket left, don't see him returning on the field.

Not out! Skidding away from the batsman outside off, Bishoo tries to play the reverse sweep but fails to connect. He loses his balance a bit as well and Rahim is quick to take the bails off. He appeals and the square leg umpire signals upstairs. The replays show that DB never left his crease.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Stumping appeal has been taken upstairs.
Spinning back in from around off, Bishoo plays it towards mid-wicket.
Stays on the back foot and helps it through the gap on the leg side for a run.

FOUR! Boom! Slower delivery again. On a length around off and is picking by Bishoo who hammers it down through mid on for a boundary. Ends his spell with a boundary but what an effort from Mortaza. Coming off a surgery and delivering straightaway, 10-1-37-4!
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Alzarri Joseph is the last batsman.

OUT! Wicket number 4 for the inspirational skipper. He certainly has made this team look like a completely different unit. Another slower delivery has fooled the batsman. Nurse spots the opportunity to swing his blade across the line since the line is quite wide outside off. But he gets tricked by the slowness of the delivery. Just like Russell did, he also spoons a catch towards long on and Mahmudullah is not dropping it. Just one more needed to take the series lead.
Plays it with gentle hands to mid-wicket, no one inside the ring and they pinch a couple of runs.
Straighter in line, this time Bishoo flicks it through square leg and picks up a single.
Full and angling into the batsman, it's flicked behind square leg for a run.
Powerplay number 3 begins. A maximum of 5 fielders allowed outside the ring now. 112 needed off 60 but two wickets look more likely.
Flatter and shorter on off, Bishoo rocks back and pushes it off the outside half of the bat to covers.
Flighted and on middle, Bishoo helps it through square leg and rushes back for the second run.
Turns it off his pads through mid-wicket and rotates the strike.
Knocks a full ball down to long on for one.
Tickles it off his pads through the leg side. Finds the gap at mid-wicket and crosses.
Flighted ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on.
Back of a length ball on middle and off, defended off the back foot.
Devendra Bishoo is the new batsman.

OUT! Mortaza strikes again. He is a very clever bowler. Knows that the batsman will be looking to go after him. Takes the pace off the ball and delivers it with a scrambled seam. Russell exposes all his stumps and then tries to yank it over the leg side. Fails to time it properly due to the lack of pace and balloons his shot high in the air. Mahmudullah settles underneath it at long on and rest is history. This in all likelihood is the last nail in the coffin for the home team.
Slower bouncer this time, Russell allows it through thinking it to be too high. One for the over, signals the square leg umpire.
Brilliantly bowled. A clever slower delivery, on a length around middle and angling down, Russell is way too early into his shot and misses.
Fetches a full ball from outside off and tries to slog it over mid-wicket. But it comes off the inner half and rolls in the deep. Only a single results and Nurse isn't happy with himself.
On a length and outside off, Nurse gets forward to play inside the line but misses.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery as he attempts to guide it down towards third man.

FOUR! That's murdered! Nearly takes the heads of the non-striker and the umpire along with it. Once again Dre Russ attacks the length ball outside off with all his might. Hammers it straight back and it whizzes past Nurse and the umpire. Reaches the fence in the blink of an eye. Sheer power. Game on as long as Russell is alive in this chase! 11 from the over, so far.

SIX! That's gigantic! They will take some time to find the ball. Rahman angles across a length ball outside off, Russell clears his front leg, fetches it from there and launches it massively over mid-wicket. On the roof and out of the stadium. 104m on the radar.
A length ball on the pads, nudged fine down the leg side for a run.
Ashley has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller and outside off, driven straight to the cover fielder.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Ashley Nurse is in next.

OUT! Mortaza gets his revenge next ball. Foxes his counterpart with an off pace delivery. Serves it on a length around off and Holder is early into his attempted heave across the line. Gets a big top edge and it loops in the air behind the bowler. Mosaddek runs back a bit from mid off and then moves across to his right to take the skier safely. Bangladesh are on the march, just 3 away from tasting their first win on a hapless tour for them thus far.
SIX! Captain v Captain and Holder has clubbed this one. Mortaza is on the shorter side around off, at his pace it's bread and butter as Jason powers it over wide long on.
Back of a length ball on off, Russell stays leg side of this one and hammers it down to long on for one. Asking rate is now 10 an over.
Picks a short ball from outside off and heaves it over mid-wicket for a single.
Short in length and outside off, Russell rocks back and scythes it over backward point for a run.
Good length delivery outside off, Andre punches it to sweeper cover and gets off the mark with a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Rock solid! Full length ball outside off, Russell blocks it with the full face of the bat to mid off.
Andre Russell arrives and will face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! Caught behind! Plenty of 'Fizz' on this delivery. Zipping away off the turf after landing on a length outside off, Powell with a tentative footwork has a poke inside the line and gets a faint outside edge behind to Rahim. The catch is taken and Rahman is on fire. Windies dwindling in this run chase.
Rovman Powell is the new batsman.

OUT! The set batsman is removed from the crease. Timely breakthrough for Bangladesh. We have seen many times in the past that a break in play brings a wicket. Hetmyer is dejected as he trudges back to the pavilion. Rahman slants in a back of a length delivery around middle, Shimron shimmies down the track attempting a big shot but is too close to the line of the ball. He still goes on with his shot and ends up chipping a straightforward catch to Shakib Al Hasan at extra cover. He makes no mistake and Windies lose their fifth wicket.
Full and angling away from the batsman, Holder strides forward and drives it down through mid off for a run.
Mustafizur Rahman is back into the attack.

Drinks break. 1 run from the last over, 20 in the last 5, Bangladesh are keeping a tight lid on the scoring rate. The required run rate is now 9.33. Pressure mounting on the hosts. 140 needed off 90 balls. Hetmyer holds the key as he has got accustomed to the pitch. In Andre Russell they possess a deadly weapon but the current partnership will have to take it deeper. Exciting finish on the cards if that happens.
Good length ball on off, stroked off the back foot to covers. Tidy stuff.
Play and a miss! Shortish and outside off, angling away, Shimron tries hacking it over the leg side but misses.
Back of a length delivery on off, it's punched off the back foot towards point.
Stifled appeal for an lbw. Good length ball landing around off, angling down, Holder tries to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. It deflects towards third man and they cross.
On a length again, around off and Holder this time makes room to stroke it through the line. However, he once again finds the cover fielder.
Starts with a length ball outside off, Jason stands back and pushes it towards the cover fielder.
Mashrafe Mortaza returns to have another go.
Quicker again, on off, defended off the back foot. 6 from this over.
Shortish and on off, punched wide of the cover fielder for a single.
Holder has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Loopy and full on middle, Shimron kneels and sweeps it over backward square leg. Decent enough connection but it doesn't go all the way. The fielder in the deep collects it on one bounce and they cross for a run.
Quicker one on off, punched back to the bowler.

Three wides! Spinning down the leg side, Hetmyer tries to sweep but misses. It goes past Rahim and Mahmudullah chases it down from short fine leg. Pulls it back and seems to have hurt himself in the process. Still saves a few runs.
Uses his long reach and drives a full ball to sweeper cover for a single.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single. End of Mehidy's spell, 10-0-37-1...he has done his job quite efficiently.
Punched off the back foot to long on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Tossed up ball on middle, flicked with the spin in front of square leg for one.

That will do. A single down to long on to bring up his maiden ODI half ton. He has a century to his name as well. Still a long way to go in this chase though. Lots of runs there to be scored and he needs to carry on.
Flatter and on off, Shimron punches it towards covers, finds the fielder.
Driven towards the mid on region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Darts it in, around off, Hetmyer tries flicking but closes the face of the bat early. It goes off the leading edge to covers.
Goes down on one knee to sweep but finds short fine leg.
Fires it in on off, Hetmyer punches it towards the cover fielder.

FOUR! Lovely footwork by Shimron. Spots the shorter delivery early, goes deep inside the crease and crunches his square cut past the point fielder. It appeared that the fielder got some hand on it but still it races away to the fence.
Flatter and on off, helped in front of square leg but the mid-wicket fielder quickly  gets to the ball.
Wide! Spinning down the leg side, Hetmyer attempts to sweep but misses.
Flighted and full outside off, Holder drives it through covers for a run.
Flatter on off, stroked from the crease but once again to the cover fielder. Excellent over, just 2 runs from it.
Walks forward and pushes it to covers again. Not in the gap.
Flatter on off, punched towards the cover fielder.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. One run added to the total.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Tossed up ball on middle, tucked through mid-wicket for a run.
Fires this one in and Shimron eases it in front of square leg for a run.

FOUR! Hetmyer uses his feet this time to a full ball and clobbers it down the ground for a boundary. The long off fielder had no chance of cutting it off. That was ferociously struck. Interesting observation by Ian Bishop on air, he mentions that before this ball Rahim had warned Shakib that the big shot is coming. Hmm...
Knocks a full ball down to long on for a run.
Full and on middle, worked past mid-wicket this time and they crossed for one.
Helps it off his pads to the leg side but finds mid-wicket.
Hetmyer has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Finds the gap this time with his punch shot. Through covers it goes and they cross.
Shortish and on off, punched to covers this time.
Gets on the back foot and punches it towards Shakib.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Jason Holder is in next.

OUT! Sharp catch and Rahim takes no chance as he does the stumping as well. A flighted off spinner, landing around off and not spinning much. Mohammed hurries down the track and tries to heave it over the leg side. His intention is to go with the spin which is minimal on this occasion and hence as a result he gets a thick outside edge behind. Rahim catches the ball and then inflicts the stumping. For a moment, I thought it's just a stumping then wondered how come the ball spun away from an offie. Mehidy doesn't possess a doosra as far as I know. The replays however confirm about the edge. Windies continue to lose wickets at regular intervals.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Another arm ball, around off and skidding in, Jason gets deep inside the crease to play the square cut but somehow manages to keep it out off the outside edge. It rolls wide of the short third man fielder and they cross.
Gets on the back foot and punches it to the cover fielder.
Tossed up ball on off, driven back to the bowler.
Flighted and on middle, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Drills a full ball right back towards the bowler who uses his boots to block it.
Arm ball on middle, Jason leans forward in defense but it goes off the inside half of the bat to square leg for a run.
Shakib Al Hasan is introduced into the attack. 172 needed off 138 balls.
Shortish and outside off, a late cut through backward point for a brace.
Goes on the back foot and hits it square of the wicket on the off side for a single.
Full and on off, knocked down to long on for one.
Fires this one in, fuller in length, Hetmyer gets on the front foot and defends it back.
Loopy and on off, on the shorter side, Shimron goes back and plays it down to point.
Shortish and outside off, cut through point for a run.
Mehidy Hasan is back on. He was brilliant in his first spell, 6-0-23-0.

FOUR! Nicely played! Once again Mosaddek is on the shorter side with his length. It's around off and skidding in. Hetmyer uses the depth of his crease and cracks it behind backward point for a boundary. Both teams going neck and neck at this stage.
Flatter on off, punched firmly to covers where the fielder made a fine stop. No chance for a run as it went quickly to him.
Too full in length and on off, drilled to deep cover-point for a run.
Goes deep inside the crease and steers it through point for a run.
Dances down the track and tries to hit it to long off. However, the extra cover fielder dives across to his left to make the stop.
Floated and full on middle, Jason paddle sweeps it to fine leg for a single.
Good length ball on off, Hetmyer covers the line and defends it back from the crease.
Fullish and around off, it's stroked off the front foot through cover-point for one.
The batsman guides it to third man. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Beautifully played. Fractionally overpitched by Rahman, it's around off and Hetmyer strokes it nicely through mid on for a boundary.
Full and on off, defended back to the bowler.
A length ball outside off, Hetmyer slices his drive through backward point and picks up a couple of runs.
Spinning back in from around middle, Jason goes deep inside the crease and punches it towards the bowler.
Full and on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Flatter and on off, punched from deep inside the crease to deep cover for a couple of runs.
Gets on the front foot and defends it with the spin to mid-wicket.

Slower through the air, full and on off, spinning back in a touch, Jason presses forward and defends it off the inner half of the bat to mid-wicket. Hetmyer looks for a run but his partner ain't interested.
Loopy full ball on middle, it's driven down the ground with the spin to long off. A single taken.
Bowls it full and around off, Jason is on the front foot trying to push it through covers but it takes the inside half of the bat and rolls back to the bowler.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Back of a length delivery on off, Hetmyer stays back and taps it down to point.
Full and angling away from the batsman, Jason reaches out for it and pushes it towards the gap at covers for a single.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Angling into the batsman from a length around off, Hetmyer defends it off his back foot.
Jason has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. 2 runs and a wicket from this over.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Leans forward to a full ball but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Jason Mohammed is the new batsman.

OUT! Gayle is run out! A critical blow to Windies. The Jamaican was very proactive in taking singles in this innings and eventually that keenness has cost him his wicket. A tossed up delivery around off, spinning away a bit, Hetmyer this time leans forward in defense and it goes off the outside half of the bat to short third man. Gayle sets off in search of a run, it's always a non-striker's call in such cases but his partner is not sure and stays at his crease. Chris has no option but to return but before he could do that, Mahmudullah has fired in the throw to the bowler who just flicks it onto the stumps. Gayle ain't in the frame and Bangladesh are delighted. The hosts need one less than 200 off 171 balls.
Fine delivery. Gripping off the surface and turning away from the batsman from around off, Hetmyer stays back to defend but gets beaten.
Too full in length and outside off, Gayle drives it down the ground to long off for a single.
A touch short in length, landing around off and cutting back in a bit, Shimron tries hitting it through the line but gets cramped up a shade. Ends up mistiming his shot to covers.
Hetmyer has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Width on offer outside off, Gayle guides it down to third man and crosses.
Again a full length ball is sliding down the leg side, Hetmyer clips it through square leg for one.
This one is full and outside off, it's driven past the right side of the bowler to long off for a single.
Starts with a full ball angling into the batsman, Gayle flicks it off his pads but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
First look of Mustafizur Rahman.
Hetmyer has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tries sweeping this one but fails to make proper connection. It goes off his pads to hit him on the body.
Tossed up ball outside off, Hetmyer outside edges his attempted drive down to third man for a couple of runs.
Driven towards the mid on region. One run added to the total.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Gayle has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Straighter in line, worked off the pads to mid-wicket.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. One run added to the total.

Good length ball on off, Hetmyer punches it towards covers and sets off for a single. The throw comes to the striker's end where Gayle lifts his bat and allows the ball through. Could have been risky but the Jamaican was safely in.

Ouch, that would have hurt Hetmyer. What was Mosaddek aiming at? A length ball on off, Gayle taps it down towards short third man and crosses for a quick run. Mosaddek attacks the ball and rather than aiming at the stumps he ends up aiming at the batsman who was running quite wide. Shimron cops a blow on his body but doesn't show much pain
Stays on the back foot and punches it square of the wicket on the off side for a run.
Good length ball on middle and off, Gayle is squared up a bit and gets it away on the off side. It rolls towards the cover region and they cross.
Taps a length ball towards the cover region for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter and on off, defended off the back foot.
Driven towards the mid on region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Flatter and shorter on off, cut from the back foot to point.

Drinks break. The going so far has been slow from the Windies and they have lost a couple of wickets as well. Bangladesh would believe that they have the upper hand at the moment but with Chris Gayle in the middle, they can least afford to relax. The Jamaican has adopted a different approach today and is concentrating more on singles rather than the big shots. Let's see how the next phase pans out.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Plays a length ball down towards wide mid on.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Forces a full ball down to mid off for a run. Another quick single.

SIX! Shot! A length ball around off, right in the arc for the batsman, Gayle prods forward and hammers it over mid off for his second biggie of the innings. The last one was also hit in the same region.
Good length ball outside off, Gayle dabs it down to the right side of the point fielder who dives over the ball and concedes an extra run. Two added to the total.
Quicker on off, Hetmyer walks forward and gets an inside edge onto the pads.

NOT OUT! A slider by Hossain, around off and skidding back in, Gayle uses his feet and tries to knock it down the ground but fails to middle his shot properly. It appears to have hit the pad first and then the bat and as a result the Bangladesh players appeal. The umpire remains unmoved and this time Mortaza consults his bowler rather than Rahim (who got it wrong the last time) before signalling for the DRS. The replays roll in, they confirm that the ball has hit the pad first and then show it to be clipping the leg stump. Umpire's call. With the batsman so much down the track, it's always a dicey call to take the review. Anyway, they don't lose it. The batsmen cross which was initially given as a leg bye but then corrected to a run.
Huge scream for an lbw! Not given again and Mortaza consults his bowler before taking the DRS.
Advances down the track and forces a full ball through mid off for a run.
Shimron has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy and on off, it's been driven off the front foot back towards the bowler.
Gets forward to a full ball and drives it with the spin to point.
Plays a length ball towards point for a single. 7 from the over.
FOUR! Short in length on middle, Hetmyer swivels on the back foot and pulls it powerfully to the deep mid-wicket fence.
A length ball on off has been defended by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Gets forward to push it towards mid off for a sharp single.
Beaten on the drive. Full and outside off, moving away, Gayle tries to drive off the front foot but misses.
Shortish and on middle, played in the gap at mid-wicket for one.
Stays back to a shortish ball and punches it down to long on for a single.
Tossed up ball on off, defended from the crease by Shimron.
Knocks a full ball down to long on for a run.
Loopy around off, Gayle has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat
Flighted on off, blocked off the front foot.
Wide! Fires one down the leg side, Gayle tries to flick but misses.
Mosaddek Hossain to bowl now.
Aahhh...nearly chops it on. A length ball outside off, Gayle pushes at it with an angled bat and gets an inside edge. It runs past the stumps to fine leg and they cross for a single.
Fullish and outside off, driven through covers for one.
Slower in pace this time, Gayle tries to drive but is late into it. It takes the outside half of the bat and speeds past backward point for a run.
Excellent delivery, shaping away from the batsman, Gayle pushes at it and misses.
In the channel outside off, Hetmyer pushes at it and edges it down to third man for a run.
Shimron Hetmyer is the new batsman.

OUT! Rubel strikes first ball! Shai is trapped in front. A delivery in line of the stumps, angling in and Hope tries to flick it on the leg side after shuffling across the line. Misses to get rapped on the pads, they let out a huge cry in lbw and up goes the finger. Hope has a little chat with Gayle who advises not to take the DRS. Now then, the replays show that it's missing leg. Two balls and two wrong calls. One benefiting Windies another benefiting Bangladesh. 239 needed off 227 balls.
Rubel Hossain is the first bowling change.

Huge shout for an lbw! Not given and Rahim advises against taking the DRS. Dear me, the replays later on show that it's hit Gayle in line and is going on to hit the leg stump. Big reprieve for the Jamaican. It's a slider around off, skidding in and catching Gayle on the front pad who failed to put bat on ball in his attempted forward defense. The bowler was interested in taking the review but the keeper wasn't of the same opinion. Hmm...
Leans forward to a full ball and gets an inside edge onto the pads.

SIX! The giant has woken up from his slumber. Floated full outside off, enough room there for Gayle to exercise his arms and he spanks it over mid off for a maximum. With this biggie, Gayle now tops the list for most runs in Bangladesh-Windies ODIs.
Darts one in, from around off, a slider, Gayle is forward again and plays it off his pads to the leg side. Had he missed that, he was a plumb lbw candidate.
Beaten! Slower through the air, full and just outside off, Gayle is on the front foot in defense but it spins away slightly to beat the outside edge.
Loopy and on middle, it's eased off the pads through backward square leg for a single.
A back foot defense on the off side to complete another tidy over by Mortaza.
Shortish and on middle, an off pace delivery, Gayle taps it down to point and looks for a run. Is sent back as the fielder quickly gets to the ball.
Length ball angling away from the batsman, Gayle gets forward and pushes it with an angled bat towards point.
Works it in front of square leg and crosses for a run.
Stays back to a length ball and pushes it towards point.
Full and angling into the batsman on middle, Shai flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Powerplay 2 time! A maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the 40th over. Mortaza to continue...
Hope has driven it through mid on. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Quietly plays it off his pads to the gap on the leg side and crosses.
Goes on the back foot and works it with the spin through mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted and full on off, Hope is on the front foot this time as he pushes it back to Mehidy.
Flatter off spinner, landing around off, Shai gets on the back foot punches it towards the bowler.
Gets on the front foot and drives it through mid off for a run.
Another back foot defense by Hope to end the over. Just a run and a wicket off it, top stuff.
Good length ball on off, blocked off the back foot.
Shai Hope is the new batsman.

OUT! Mortaza strikes to draw first blood. Switches to 'round the wicket for Lewis and delivers a seam up delivery. It's on a good length outside off and angles towards the off stumps. Lewis stands back to hammer it over the mid off fielder but fails to get the proper connection on it. Ends up hitting it towards Mahmudullah who backtracks just slightly to catch the ball which had some velocity behind it. Completes it with a tumble and the Bangladesh players celebrate.
Some extra bounce this time from a length around middle, Gayle pushes it gently to mid off for a single.
Fullish and outside off, driven off the front foot to covers.

Comprehensively beaten! Gayle is itching to dominate Mortaza but the latter has won the battle so far. A smart off cutter around off, not picked by Chris who shapes up for an ugly hoick over the leg side but only to get beaten.
Quicker delivery, darted in around off, Lewis decided to play at it from the back foot and just about managed to keep it out at the last moment. That delivery was heading for the sticks.
Goes on the back foot and punches it back to the bowler.
Tossed up ball on middle, swept across the line but straight to short fine leg.
Flatter and quicker on off, Lewis remains on the back leg as he defends it out safely.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Due to the misfield. Flighted full ball outside off, Lewis drills his drive through the line and the cover fielder makes a meal out of a simple stopping chance. He moves across to his right but fails to stop the ball. It sneaks past him and races away to the fence in no time. Rahim is disappointed.
Play and a miss! Just like the first delivery of this over. Smart variation from Mortaza. Takes the pace off the delivery and serves it full and outside off. Gayle swishes and misses.
Lets out a grunt and delivers a back of a length ball in line of the stumps. Gayle is caught inside the crease, no room to work with and he defends it to the off side.
Shortish and outside off, cut from the back foot to covers.
A good length ball on off, Gayle closes the face of the bat early this time and it goes off the leading edge towards covers.

FOUR! Well played! Mortaza angles across a length ball outside off, staying a bit low as well, Gayle keeps his eyes glued to the delivery and at the last moment guides it past short third man for a boundary.
Beaten all ends up! Mortaza runs in from over the wicket and hurls across a little cutter around off. Without picking the variation, Gayle tries to flick it across the line and misses.
Quicker again, a slider on off, Lewis stays on the back foot and offers a straight bat in defense.
Flatter and on off, blocked off the back foot.
Tossed up ball but too full outside off, Lewis plays a thunderous drive but finds the cover fielder.
Flighted and outside off, left alone.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.

FOUR! Great start to the over for Windies. Hasan bowls it flat and full around middle and leg. Lewis kneels and sweeps it across the line. It screams past the right side of the backward square leg fielder for a boundary.
A length ball angling into the southpaw, Lewis sticks back to push it towards mid off and crosses for a sharp single. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. A tidy over.
Once again hangs back inside the crease and pushes it firmly through the line. Finds the extra cover fielder. Another dot.
Good length ball on off, angling in, it's punched off the back foot but straight to the cover fielder.
Play and a miss! Mortaza continues from 'round the wicket and serves a length ball outside off, a little change in pace probably. Lewis stands back to throw his bat at it but fails to connect.
Hits this length ball back towards the bowler.

Gayle is eyeing singles. That's a very rare sight. Maybe, warming up his inside monster. Bunts this ball down the ground, towards mid off and takes a brisk single. Also, maybe he doesn't want his partner to be strike-deprived as Lewis usually loses his patience when that happens.
Forces a shortish ball around off to covers.
Gets down on one knee to play the sweep shot but fails to connect properly. A stifled appeal follows as the batsmen cross. It's given as runs and the replays detect some gloves on it.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. No run.
Skidding back in, from around off, Gayle gets it away off the inside half of the bat to the leg side. In the gap it goes and they pinch a single.
Fires this one on off, Gayle pushes it with an angled bat to backward point.
Flighted and on off, defended off the front foot to the off side.

SIX! That's high and handsome! Mortaza is on the shorter side, around middle at a gentle pace, Lewis easily gets inside the crease, turns a bit in his stance and smashes it over mid-wicket for a maximum. Spoils a good over.
Shortish and on off, not enough room, Lewis punches from the crease to covers.
The mid on drops back before this delivery and Mortaza lands it on a length around middle and off. Gayle punches it towards covers and crosses for a run.
Gayle has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Stays back to play down a length ball towards point.
Full and on middle, defended down towards mid on.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and on middle, pushed down to mid on.

Chance of a run out! A better throw would have made things interesting. A flighted ball around off, Gayle leans forward and pushes it off the shoulder of the bat towards short third man. He sets off for a run but is ball-watching at the same time. His partner is waiting for the signal and Gayle gives one after coming mid-way down the track. Now Lewis wears his skates and hurries across to the other end. Rubel sends across a wayward throw, Rahim collects it far from the stumps and then tries to back-flick towards them and connects. However, Lewis is safely in by then. Nervy moment for the Windies.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Fires this one down the leg side, Gayle flicks it off his pads but finds the fine leg fielder.
Beaten! Tossed up ball just around off, not turning much, Gayle gets forward to play inside the line but misses.

Not a surprise as there is a spinner bowling from the other end. Mehidy Hasan to bowl to the two left-handers in the middle. The Windies' spinners got good spin from the surface, let's see how he fares. A slip in place.
And again. Another good looking shot through the line gets stopped by the fielder at covers. Not a clean one but good enough to keep it to dot.
A back foot punch to a length ball outside off but once again he finds the cover fielder.
Full length ball angling away from the batsman, Lewis pushes it from the crease to covers.
Straighter in line, a well-timed flick shot by Evin but he finds the square leg fielder.
A sight to behold! Gayle pushes a full ball around middle and off towards short cover and scampers off to the other end. First run is always vital.
Starts with a length ball around leg, Gayle taps it down off his pads to mid-wicket.
Back for the run chase! Chris Gayle and Evin Lewis are the Windies' openers. Mashrafe Mortaza to kickoff proceedings with a slip in place. Here we go...
